_readme: THE DUTY MATRIX — [pipeline K-13] Private/requirements/ (was pipeline/08-compliance-legal.md, folded into the JSON spec 2026-08-15)
One row per compliance duty this factory has taken on: what it is, whether it is implemented, WHAT
WOULD TRIGGER IT if it is not, and where the claim came from. A tripwire with no stateable trigger is
decoration; a duty with no source is somebody's memory.
🔴 NOBODY HERE IS A LAWYER, AND THIS FILE DOES NOT PRETEND OTHERWISE. Rows record what can be
OBSERVED — which artefact exists, which guard runs, which page publishes what — and, where a duty
rests on an external rule, the PRIMARY SOURCE it was read from and the date it was read. Where a rule
could not be read from a primary source in this environment, the row says COULD-NOT-ESTABLISH and
names what would have to be read. It is NEVER given a plausible-looking number or a plausible URL.
An invented figure in a compliance rule fires on CORRECT input while looking authoritative — a
made-up '120 characters or fewer' once rejected this repo's own fixture at 129, and the fix was to
delete the number, not to adjust it.
🔴 THE SOURCE-HOST ALLOWLIST IS THE HIGHEST-VALUE RULE IN THIS FILE, and it is four lines of code.
A row's source URL must be a REGULATOR, a LEGISLATURE or a STORE/PLATFORM's own documentation. A
law-firm page, a compliance vendor's blog, a summary site or a news article FAILS THE ROW. Roughly
thirty dead claims entered this project's corpus because a compliance-vendor blog said so, and every
one of them read as authoritative. See `sourceHosts` below for the list and the reasoning.
⚠️ THE COVERAGE SET IS THE REQUIREMENT LIST BELOW, AND IT IS INCOMPLETE BY CONSTRUCTION. K-13's
acceptance asks for the stage's 16 requirement ids PLUS its 14 written cuts. The written cuts live in

Private/requirements/not-built.json as its `[8]cut 1` … `[8]cut 14` entries (the stage prose that wrote them was folded into the JSON spec 2026-08-15), and Private/ is gitignored — CI cannot read it, and a row
set derived from a file no guard can open would be a coverage claim over nothing (the exact defect
that stopped the previous increment). So the declared set here is the requirement ids, in-tree, and
this limitation is written down rather than papered over. See tooling/legal/README.md.
🔴 THE MARKET VOCABULARY IS NOT DECLARED ANYWHERE. IT IS THE UNION OF THE `markets` ARRAYS ON THE
ROWS BELOW, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE POINT. [pipeline K-1] A stamped app declares the markets it is
offered in, and hooks/pre_gen.dart resolves each declared token against these rows: a token no row
names resolves to ZERO duties and the stamp is REFUSED by name. A separate list of 'markets we
support' would be a second declaration and the first to drift — somebody adds `global` to it, every
stamp passes, and `global` means nothing at all. Here a market can only become declarable by adding
the row that makes a duty resolvable in it, which is the work rather than a line in a list.
⚠️ A ROW IS TAGGED ONLY WHERE IT ALREADY NAMED ITS JURISDICTION IN ITS OWN TEXT — the DPDP rows say
India, the AI-Act row cites eur-lex, the GPC row is sourced to oag.ca.gov (California, hence `us-ca`
and not `us`: the row is about a Californian rule and tagging it `us` would be the invented-scope
failure this file opens by warning about). AN UNTAGGED ROW IS NOT 'GLOBAL' — it is a row nobody has
scoped, and deciding which markets a duty reaches is a legal judgement no one here is qualified to
make. That is why resolution counts TAGGED rows only: the honest reading of `in` resolving to three
rows is 'this repo has done market-specific work for India', not 'these are all the duties in India'.
Enforced by tooling/ci/assert-legal-tripwires.mjs:
· every declared requirement has at least one row; every row names a declared requirement  [K-13.1]
· every source URL's host is on the allowlist                                              [K-13.2]
· every row carries a status from the declared vocabulary AND a stateable trigger          [K-13.3]
· a PASSED reviewBy date FAILS; owner-gated rows PRINT rather than fail                    [K-13.4]
· a COULD-NOT-ESTABLISH row may NOT carry a source URL — that is what the mark MEANS       [risk 6]
· a row claiming `implemented` names an artefact that must EXIST in the tree               [K-13.1]
· COVERAGE LOST on an empty matrix or an empty requirement list                            [F-10]

_why: REGULATORS, LEGISLATURES AND THE PLATFORM'S OWN DOCUMENTATION. Nothing else.
The test each host passes: it is the body that WROTE the rule, or the platform that ENFORCES it.
A law firm's client alert, a compliance SaaS blog, a 'GDPR checklist' site and a news report all
fail it — not because they are always wrong, but because a claim sourced to one cannot be
re-verified, and a compliance corpus is only as good as its ability to be re-checked later.
developer.android.com and partner.microsoft.com are here on the same footing as
developer.apple.com and support.google.com: they are the store's own publication of its own rule,
which is the enforcing body speaking. A store's requirement is not a law, and rows sourced to one
say so in their `duty` text rather than borrowing the authority of a statute.

statuses._why: The vocabulary rows are validated against, in the register rather than in the guard so that renaming one out from under the rows using it fails.
statuses.implemented: an artefact in this tree discharges it, and the row names that artefact.
statuses.partial: some limbs are built and the row says which are not.
statuses.not-started: nothing built. The row's trigger is what makes it surface at the right moment.
statuses.owner-gated: blocked on a decision or an account only the owner can supply. PRINTS every run, never fails the build.
statuses.watching: no duty today; the row exists so the trigger is written down instead of remembered.

verificationKinds.primary-source: read from the body that wrote or enforces the rule. Requires `source.url` on the allowlist and a `fetched` date.
verificationKinds.in-tree: verifiable inside this repository — a guard, a file, a workflow step. No external source applies.
verificationKinds.decision: settled by a decision record of ours. `decisionRecord` names it; CI cannot open it (`Private/` is gitignored — this said `knowledge/` under the pre-2026-08-15 layout, and the flatten merged that directory into `Private/`; the same rename applies to the two other rows below that say this), so it is a pointer, not an assertion.
verificationKinds.COULD-NOT-ESTABLISH: the rule could not be read from a primary source in this environment. MUST NOT carry a source URL. `wouldNeed` says what would have to be read.

_why: The declared coverage set. A duty with no row FAILS and a row naming no duty FAILS, so this is a
RELATIONSHIP rather than a count somebody lowers — deleting an id here is deleting the duty, which
is a visible act, and adding one immediately demands a row.
requirements.K-1: Every app declares the markets it is offered in
requirements.K-2: The legal document set is published and cannot vanish silently
requirements.K-2a: A pricing page exists, is navigation-linked, and terms names the seller
requirements.K-3: Every published legal claim is asserted true of the code
requirements.K-4: The exact text a user consented to is retrievable forever
requirements.K-5: The commercial surface names the actual seller and payment path
requirements.K-6: Every app links its own legal surface in-app
requirements.K-7: The erasure path is published, reachable and not orphaned
requirements.K-8: One declared personal-data inventory behind every disclosure
requirements.K-9: A rights complaint is actionable in hours without a store release
requirements.K-10: Rights evidence for every third-party asset shipped
requirements.K-11: The in-app licences surface covers what the app ships
requirements.K-12: The repository's own legal posture is stated
requirements.K-13: The per-market duty matrix cannot silently rot
requirements.K-14: The notice is intelligible in the user's language, on demand
requirements.K-15: Web builds honour the Global Privacy Control signal
requirements.K-16: No kids app without the children's surface

duties.duty: A stamped app declares which markets it is offered in, so a per-market duty can be resolved mechanically rather than remembered.
duties.trigger: The day a second app is stamped. A market field added after five apps exist is five retrofits plus notices already published without it.
duties.note: BUILT 2026-08-07. brick.yaml declares `markets` and hooks/pre_gen.dart refuses a stamp that declares none — atomically, because a throwing pre_gen makes mason exit 64 having written nothing. The SECOND limb is what stops the declaration being decorative: each declared token is resolved against the `markets` arrays on the rows in this file, and a token that resolves to ZERO rows is refused by name with the resolvable set printed, so `global` cannot quietly mean nothing. post_gen writes the resolved list into the app's catalogue row, so the declaration outlives the stamp. NOT BUILT: apps/subly predates the var and its catalog/apps.json row carries no `markets` — WHICH markets a shipped app is offered in is the owner's commercial call, and a value invented here would be exactly the plausible-looking figure this file's own preamble forbids.

duties.duty: privacy, terms and refund resolve on the site that fronts every published app, and cannot be deleted silently.
duties.trigger: Already live. The tripwire is the guard itself: deleting a page fails the build instead of surfacing as a store takedown.

duties.duty: Every store channel requires a reachable privacy-policy URL in its console before a product that touches personal information can be published. This is a STORE requirement, not a statute.
duties.trigger: Already in force for any channel we submit to. apps/*/store/*/privacy-policy-url.txt carries the URL and check-site-integrity.mjs proves it resolves to a page this repo serves.

source.quote: Microsoft Store Policies §10.5.1 — a privacy policy URL is required in Partner Center for any product that accesses personal information. Recorded in Private/requirements/ledger.json, entry [10]D-4, against that fetch.

duties.duty: A published price list, which a store reviewer and a merchant-of-record seller verification both look for.
duties.trigger: Before the first paid product goes live, or before a merchant-of-record application is submitted.
duties.note: The prices are already decided; only the copy and the go-live are outstanding. check-site-integrity.mjs PRINTS the missing page every run and flips to a 'PROMOTE ME' notice the moment it lands.

duties.duty: Every emphasised claim on a published legal page is paired to what makes it true, and the ones that can be checked against code are.
duties.trigger: Already live. Publishing a new emphasised sentence fails the build until it is paired.

duties.duty: Before any first-party promotional surface renders in a shipped app, the privacy notice states the legal basis for it, names the objection right and where the switch is, and the advertising sentence separates our own promotion from third-party ad networks.
duties.trigger: 🔴 THE DAY A PROMOTIONAL SURFACE RENDERS TO A REAL USER IN A SHIPPED BUILD — not the day the component is written, and not the day a config key exists. [ADR 040] makes the published section THE gate on that surface. SATISFIED 2026-08-10, AHEAD OF THE TRIGGER, WHICH IS THE ORDER THIS ROW ALWAYS ASKED FOR: §3 of the notice was published on owner signature while every promo surface is still dormant (features.promo_card_enabled is absent from every served config, and an absent key reads false). ⚠️ THE ROW STAYS IN THE MATRIX BECAUSE THE DUTY IS CONTINUOUS, NOT DISCHARGED: the day the flag is armed is the day somebody must re-read §3 against what actually renders. And the trigger still cannot be detected by the guard that sounds like it should — the advertising claim row in tooling/legal/policy-claims.json asserts `absent` over every pubspec.yaml, so it keys on a DEPENDENCY, and a house-ad surface adds none.
duties.decisionRecord: Private/decisions/040-cross-promo-v1-lock.md — LOCKED 2026-08-10, decision 3: 'D2 (privacy-policy legal-basis section) is drafted, not flipped. ADR 031 class B stands: the agent produces the ready-to-sign diff; the section goes live only on owner signature. It remains THE gate on any promo surface rendering.' SIGNED 2026-08-10. The reasoning is Private/research/44-CROSS-PROMOTION-HOUSE-ADS-OFFERS.md V2/V3/V4; the diff that was signed is docs/legal/privacy-direct-marketing-draft.md.
duties.note: PUBLISHED 2026-08-10 as privacy.html §3 'Offers and promotions inside our apps', at policy version 2026-08-10. The signature is the version bump, and it moved in three places at once (the page's data-policy-version and visible date, kPrivacyPolicyVersion in apps/subly, and the same constant in the brick) plus an archive snapshot at sites/nikatru/legal/2026-08-10/en/privacy.html — because privacy.html sits inside the policy-VERSION surface and assert-policy-archive.mjs / assert-seams-wired.mjs make a partial application impossible rather than merely inadvisable. The advertising sentence was narrowed in the same commit to 'no Nikatru app carries third-party advertising', its policy-claims.json row and apps/subly/store/android-play/ads-declaration.json moved with it (they are pinned by exact string equality), and `crossChecks.policyPage.assertsAbsence` went true → false. THAT FLIP IS WHAT OPENED THE GATE: tooling/ci/assert-ads-declarations.mjs had been failing for as long as any promo component existed in-tree beside the unqualified sentence, deliberately, and it now exits 0. ⚠️ NO GUARD ASSERTS THIS ROW'S SUBSTANCE AND NONE CAN: whether a stated legal basis is the correct one is a lawyer's judgement. What IS mechanical is the pairing (set-equality of emphasised spans to register rows), the objection control (`Offers and promotions` asserts `recordPromoObjection(` in the Settings screen) and the on-device claim (`on your device` asserts PromoGate imports nothing).

duties.duty: For every policy version that has ever been in force, the exact bytes a user consented to are still servable at a stable URL.
duties.trigger: Every version bump. The archive snapshot lands in the SAME commit as the bump — recovering the bytes only gets harder.

duties.duty: The pages a buyer reads name the actual seller and the actual payment path, and agree with each other.
duties.trigger: Before the first sale on ANY channel. terms.html and refund.html now name Paddle as the merchant of record and split the channels by who takes the payment ([ADR 039]); privacy.html §3 still describes the role without naming anybody, and that page cannot be corrected without a policy-version bump.
duties.note: The guard is built and the remaining gaps print every run (tooling/legal/provider-register.json disclosureGaps). ✅ TWO THINGS CLOSED: the `website-seller-contradiction` gap was RETIRED — the pages no longer name a gateway for a purchase privacy.html says does not happen — and the open decision this row used to carry ('which rails is a buyer offered') was ANSWERED by [ADR 039] D6 on measurement rather than preference: Paddle serves Indian buyers too, Razorpay is not the app rail. 🔴 WHAT REMAINS IS NOT WORDING. It is the seller account (A-1) and one owner signature on privacy.html, which is version-gated; the buyer-facing pages are already consistent with the register and with packages/purchases/lib/src/purchase_capabilities.dart, channel by channel. ⚠️ TWO WORDING ITEMS FOR THE OWNER'S EYE THAT WERE DELIBERATELY NOT CHANGED, because guessing at them would be worse than naming them: (1) terms.html §4 still ends 'Prices are inclusive of applicable taxes unless stated otherwise', and a merchant of record may present tax either inclusively or added at checkout depending on the buyer's country — whichever Paddle's checkout actually does for our SKUs is a LIVE-VERIFY item at A-1, not a fact this tree holds, and the bullet is left standing rather than rewritten from a guess; (2) refund.html §1 no longer lists a Microsoft order-history link, because [ADR 039] D1 puts Microsoft Store purchases on the Paddle rail and Microsoft therefore has no order to refund — the page's opening line ('who handles your refund depends on who sold you the product, and your receipt names them') is what keeps a buyer un-stranded if a store ever bills directly for a paid app listing.

duties.duty: The in-app-purchase aggregator that holds purchase state for store sales is disclosed in the privacy notice before it holds any — and is never described to a buyer as the seller, which it is not.
duties.trigger: 🔴 THE DAY ANY APP RECORDS A REAL STORE PURCHASE — i.e. the first non-sandbox event to POST /v1/webhooks/revenuecat. It is not the day the SDK is added and it is not the day a store account is created; it is the first event carrying a real person's entitlement. Nothing today can send one (every kind:store row in tooling/channel-register.json is served:false), which is precisely why this is easy to still be missing on the day something can.
duties.decisionRecord: Private/decisions/039-payment-rails-per-platform.md D5 — LOCKED 2026-08-09: RevenueCat is the mobile-store IAP glue, entering the codebase at the Play-Billing increment and at A-4.
duties.note: Two duties in one row because they fail in opposite directions and share one fact. (a) DISCLOSURE: RevenueCat holds an account identifier and entitlement records, so privacy.html §3 owes it a mention — carried as the `iap-aggregator-unnamed` gap, which prints every run. (b) THE ROLE, WHICH IS THE HALF A GUARD CAN GET WRONG FOR US: an aggregator is not a merchant of record. tooling/legal/provider-register.json keeps its `role` at `iap_aggregator`; flip that field and assert-policy-claims.mjs §3(c) would start DEMANDING that terms.html and refund.html name RevenueCat as the seller — a false disclosure the guard itself asked for. Recorded as `decision` rather than `primary-source`: what is asserted here is our own lock, and CI cannot open `Private/` (gitignored), so the pointer is data and not an assertion.

duties.duty: Every app links its own privacy, terms and refund surface from inside the app, reachable rather than merely declared.
duties.trigger: Every new stamped app. The brick ships two of the three links; nothing asserts they are reachable from a real screen.
duties.note: The property test that pumps the settings screen and taps the tile is [8]INC-5, whose files (assert-stamp-properties.mjs, settings_screen.dart, chassis_properties_test.dart) are stage 2/3 primaries — deliberately not touched in this change.

duties.duty: A user can ask for their data to be erased, from inside the app and from the public web, and the request reaches something that can act on it.
duties.trigger: 🔴 BEFORE the first app that creates an account ships to a store. The in-app control exists and the server route now exists; there is still no PUBLIC WEB deletion page, which is what a store reviewer and a non-user look for.
duties.unblocked: 🟢 [4]B-5 LANDED ON MAIN WHILE THIS MATRIX WAS BEING WRITTEN (services/platform/src/routes/account.ts, DELETE /v1/account). The stage-8 plan records this duty as BLOCKED on it and that is no longer true — recorded here rather than left standing, because a stale blocker is exactly the rot K-13 exists to catch, and 'we are blocked' is the most comfortable thing in a compliance matrix to be wrong about. What remains for K-7 is limb (b), the published web page, plus the no-orphaned-claim assertion — [8]INC-12, not built here.
duties.note: 🔴 AND A NARROWER PROBLEM THE PROMISE DOES NOT ACKNOWLEDGE: `events` and `consent_artifacts` are keyed on anon_id, so 'delete my account' provably cannot purge them. Either the published promise narrows or the client sends its anon_id on erasure. A wording decision, O-3, in the same version bump as the other corrections.

duties.duty: Every place data can be stored is enumerated, has a declared retention, and — where it holds anything about a person — quotes the published sentence that discloses it.
duties.trigger: Every new table, binding or Pages-Function store. A store with no row fails the build.
duties.note: As of 2026-08-09 THREE rows declare retention `undecided` and print every run: platform_db.provider_notifications, platform_db.unclaimed_payments and platform_db.events. Each needs a decision, not a guess. (This note previously said two and named the nikatru-signups KV as one of them: the KV's period was declared that day — 365 days, `kind: ttl`, verified against the code — and the note had already been undercounting the money-rail rows. The live list is whatever assert-data-inventory.mjs prints; this sentence is a dated snapshot of it, not a second source.)

duties.duty: A rights complaint about shipped content can be acted on in hours, without waiting for a store release.
duties.trigger: The day the first content pack ships to a real user. Until then there is nothing to take down.
duties.note: The content-pack chassis is wired but `contentPack: null` in both the brick and the one shipping app, so the emergency path has never been exercised. Making that assertion non-vacuous is [8]INC-11, whose files are stage 2/3 primaries. The DRILL itself needs the pack keypair (OWNER_QUEUE S-3) and a published pack.

duties.duty: Every asset that ships inside a build has a recorded licence, and that licence claim carries a source and a date.
duties.trigger: Every asset added to a pubspec or dropped into an assets directory. A shipped asset with no row fails the build.

duties.duty: The icon font Flutter bundles into every build under `uses-material-design: true` has a licence we can point at.
duties.trigger: Before the first store submission that ships the bundled icon font — which is every submission.
duties.wouldNeed: The LICENSE file in Google's material-design-icons repository, read directly, at the revision Flutter vendors. The stage document states CC-BY 4.0 as a headline fact; that licence was the project's EARLIER one and the repository has published under Apache-2.0 since 2016. Neither could be confirmed from a primary source in this environment, so NEITHER is recorded as the answer, and tooling/legal/asset-register.json carries the row as UNVERIFIED rather than guessing.
duties.note: 🔴 THE GUARD DESIGN SURVIVES EITHER ANSWER, which is why this is a row and not a blocker: 'fail on any bundled asset with no register row' is licence-agnostic, and the register refuses a row whose licence claim has no source.

duties.duty: Every app shows the licences of what it ships, from a real screen.
duties.trigger: Every new app. The brick ships an AboutListTile; apps/subly ships none, and that gap is printed every run.
duties.note: Closing it means editing apps/subly's settings screen, which is [8]INC-5's file and stage 2/3 territory.

duties.duty: The repository states what it is: source-visible, not open-source, with no licence grant.
duties.trigger: Already live. A LICENSE file appearing at the root fails the build — the only irreversible thing in this matrix, because a grant cannot be un-granted.
duties.decisionRecord: Private/requirements/not-built.json — 'A LICENSE file / an open-source posture for the public monorepo', decided 2026-07-20, origin 'requirements/master-requirements.md §0.1 (DECIDED 5)'. The prose master-requirements.md this field used to name was folded into the JSON spec on 2026-08-16 in commit e88fdcf; recover it with `git -C Private show e88fdcf^:requirements/master-requirements.md`

duties.duty: The duty matrix itself is checked: every duty has a row, every row has a duty, every source is primary, every tripwire has a trigger, and no review date is in the past.
duties.trigger: Already live. This row is the one that makes the file self-referential on purpose — a matrix that does not cover itself is the first row to go stale.

duties.duty: A user is shown the notice in a language they can read, at a stable URL, for every locale the app itself supports.
duties.trigger: The day a locale is added to the app. The brick already ships two (en, ta) and only one notice exists.
duties.note: 🔴 THE OWNER-GATED PART IS THE TRANSLATION, NOT THE MACHINERY. An unreviewed machine translation of a statutory notice is itself a legal-accuracy exposure, so the missing Tamil notice PRINTS (assert-policy-archive.mjs) rather than failing CI. Propose O-4: native review of the Tamil privacy notice.

duties.duty: Decide whether web builds listen for the Global Privacy Control signal, or record the cut with a trigger.
duties.trigger: 🔴 THE DAY ANY APP SERVES ADS OR SHARES DATA WITH A THIRD PARTY. GPC attaches to sale or sharing; we do neither, and the code still agrees — zero advertising SDKs repo-wide, asserted by tooling/legal/policy-claims.json over every pubspec in the tree.
duties.wouldNeed: oag.ca.gov's own text on what GPC obliges and when. Recorded as needing a DECISION rather than more research: the stage document's own conclusion is that nothing new will be learned by researching it again. Either build the listener or take the cut — either way this row carries the trigger.

duties.duty: No app is offered to children without the surface a children's audience requires.
duties.trigger: The day an app is scheduled with a children's audience, or the day a store listing selects a children's category. Both are declarations somebody makes; neither happens by accident.
duties.note: BUILT 2026-08-07 — the REFUSAL, not the surface. brick.yaml declares `audience` and hooks/pre_gen.dart refuses `audience: children` atomically. 🔴 THE VERDICT IS READ FROM THIS ROW RATHER THAN HARDCODED: the hook requires this row to be `implemented` AND to name an `artefact` that is really on disk, so the day somebody builds the surface and files it here the stamp starts accepting a kids app, with nobody having to remember to unblock it — and equally, a status flipped to `implemented` without an artefact that exists cannot buy a pass. THIS ROW DELIBERATELY CARRIES NO `artefact`: naming pre_gen.dart here would let the thing doing the refusing be mistaken for the surface being refused about. NOT BUILT: the surface itself. privacy.html today states a bare 'under the age of 13 (or the minimum age required in your country)'. Whether that number is right for a declared market depends on the market's own threshold, and the guard must assert CONSISTENCY WITH THE DECLARED MARKET ROW rather than hardcode a number — see the COULD-NOT-ESTABLISH row below. The audience var itself is [8]INC-9, in stage 3's files.

duties.duty: The age below which a user counts as a child under India's data-protection law, and what that then requires.
duties.trigger: The day a market row declares India AND an app declares a children's audience.
duties.wouldNeed: The Digital Personal Data Protection Act text on indiacode.nic.in, sections 2(f) and 9, read directly. NOT a summary, and NOT a compliance-vendor page — the whole reason for the source allowlist. ⚠️ NO NUMBER IS RECORDED HERE and none may be until the section is read: privacy.html's '13' is the number that is currently published, and asserting a different one from an unread statute would fire on correct input while looking authoritative.

duties.duty: What a data-protection notice must contain, and in which languages it must be available, under India's data-protection law.
duties.trigger: The day a user in India creates an account, or the day the first paid sale is made to an Indian buyer.
duties.wouldNeed: The DPDP Act's notice provision (section 5) on indiacode.nic.in, read directly. The current notice was written to be plain and complete rather than to a checklist nobody here has read.

duties.duty: When the rules made under India's data-protection Act actually commence, which is what turns several of these watching rows into duties.
duties.trigger: This row IS the trigger for several others. It is reviewed on the date below rather than when somebody remembers.
duties.wouldNeed: The commencement notification on meity.gov.in. Multiple dates circulate in secondary sources and none was confirmable here; recording any of them would be recording a rumour with a citation.

duties.duty: The transparency marking obligation for AI-generated content, and the date from which it bites.
duties.trigger: Already partly discharged and the trigger is generation, not publication: every generated asset keeps its provenance marking intact and is logged with model, date and prompt.
duties.wouldNeed: The Regulation's own text on eur-lex.europa.eu, Article 50 and its transitional provisions, read directly. The GRACE PERIOD specifically could not be established, so no date is recorded.
duties.note: What IS in force here regardless of the date: [ADR 019] requires the generator's own watermark to be kept intact and a PROVENANCE.json entry per asset. That is our own decision and does not depend on establishing the statutory date.

duties.duty: Google Play's declaration requirement for apps that generate AI content, and the date it takes effect.
duties.trigger: The day an app generates content at runtime (as opposed to shipping content generated once and banked), or the day a Play submission is prepared.
duties.wouldNeed: Google Play's own policy page on support.google.com for the AI-generated-content declaration and its effective date. The effective date could not be read here.

duties.duty: Both major stores may ask for evidence of rights to material an app ships, and a review can be held or an app removed while that evidence is produced.
duties.trigger: 🔴 A DEMAND ARRIVES WITHOUT WARNING AND IS ANSWERED IN HOURS OR NOT AT ALL. The register exists so the answer is a file rather than a search.
duties.wouldNeed: The exact wording and scope of Apple's App Review Guideline 5.2.2 and Google Play's intellectual-property policy, read from developer.apple.com and support.google.com. The general obligation is not in doubt; the precise 'evidence on demand' formulation could not be confirmed here, so no clause is quoted as if it had been.

duties.duty: Whether the icon font actually shipped in a release build is the whole font or a subset, which decides what the asset register must account for.
duties.trigger: The day the asset register's bundle-walking mode runs against a real release build and the enumerated set differs from the declared one.
duties.wouldNeed: Flutter's own documentation of the icon tree-shaker's scope and when it is disabled. Recorded because the register's honesty depends on it: a subset font and a whole font are different artefacts with the same filename.

duties.duty: A personal Play developer account created after a cut-off must run a closed test with a minimum number of opted-in testers for a minimum continuous period before production access is granted.
duties.trigger: 🔴 IT IS A CALENDAR, NOT A TASK. Nothing in this repository can shorten it, so it starts the day the publisher account exists — not the day the build is ready.

source.quote: at least 12 testers must be opted-in to your closed test when you apply for production access, and they must have been opted-in for the last 14 days continuously. Scope: developers with personal accounts created after November 13, 2023.

duties.duty: New apps published on Google Play must be uploaded as an Android App Bundle.
duties.trigger: Discharged and asserted: tooling/channel-register.json compares the android-play row's accepted formats to what its lane actually emits, so a lane that stops producing the .aab fails instead of surfacing at submission.

source.quote: From August 2021, new apps are required to publish with the Android App Bundle on Google Play.

duties.duty: Apps uploaded to Google Play — new apps AND updates to existing apps — must target at least a stated Android API level. This is Play's own distribution policy, not a statute; it bites at UPLOAD and the only symptom is the upload being rejected.
duties.trigger: 🔴 IT WAS UNPINNED UNTIL 2026-08-04. `targetSdk = flutter.targetSdkVersion` resolved out of the installed Flutter SDK's FlutterExtension.kt, where 3.44.x happens to declare 36 — so the app met the floor by accident of which toolchain was installed, and a Flutter downgrade would have dropped it below with no diff, no Gradle error and no failing test. Now an integer literal, and tooling/ci/assert-android-target-sdk.mjs reads `enforced.targetSdkAtLeast` from THIS row and fails the build if the literal is below it or stops being a literal.

enforced._why: The number lives HERE, beside its citation, and nowhere else. A floor hard-coded inside the guard would be a limit with no source attached — the shape assert-ceiling-budget.mjs and assert-store-metadata.mjs both refuse — and a second copy in the Gradle file would be two sources of truth for one number.

source.quote: Starting 31 August 2026, new apps and app updates must target API level 36 (Android 16) or higher; an extension to 1 November 2026 may be requested in Play Console. Wear OS / Automotive require 35, TV / XR require 34.

duties.duty: Every shared library shipped inside an artifact uploaded to Google Play must have its ELF LOAD segments aligned to at least 16 KB, so the app runs on 64-bit devices whose kernel is configured with 16 KB memory pages. This is Play's own distribution policy, not a statute; like every other row in this family it bites at UPLOAD, and the only symptom is the release being refused.
duties.trigger: 🔴 NOTHING IN THIS TREE HAD EVER LOOKED INSIDE A `.so`. Measured 2026-08-20: `readelf`, `llvm-readelf`, `objdump`, `zipalign`, `p_align` and `max-page-size` returned ZERO hits across every workflow, guard, Gradle file and script. The alignment is decided by the NDK and the linker flags Flutter's own Gradle plugin passes, so it is not a value anybody in this repository writes down — which is exactly why nothing noticed it: there is no line to review. It changes underneath the app when the toolchain moves, with no diff, no Gradle error and no failing test, the same shape as the unpinned `targetSdk` above. tooling/ci/assert-elf-page-alignment.mjs reads `enforced.loadSegmentAlignAtLeast` from THIS row and parses the ELF program headers of every `lib/*/*.so` inside the built artifact.

enforced._why: The number lives HERE, beside its citation, and nowhere else — the same reason `targetSdkAtLeast` does. 16384 is 2**14, which is the form the cited page states it in; the guard converts once and prints both, so a reader comparing the page to the output never has to do the arithmetic themselves.

source.quote: all apps targeting Android 15 (API level 35) and higher must support 16 KB memory page sizes on 64-bit devices on Google Play. Starting February 1, 2027, if your app updates don't support 16 KB memory page sizes, you won't be able to release these updates. · 16 KB devices require the shared libraries' ELF segments to be aligned properly using 16 KB ELF alignment in order for your app to run. · Check the output lines to ensure that the load segments don't have values less than 2**14.

duties.duty: Apps uploaded to App Store Connect must be built with a minimum Xcode version.
duties.trigger: Already in force, and it bites at UPLOAD — the first submission, not the first build. ⚠️ CORRECTED 2026-09-05 — the three clauses that stood here were each measured FALSE. They read: "build-platforms.yml pins no Xcode and tooling/versions.json has no xcode key; tooling/channel-register.json prints that gap every run rather than failing CI". Measured on d3469b3: tooling/versions.json:183 declares "xcode": "26" (Renovate exemption at :336); build-platforms.yml:951 runs a step named "The Xcode floor is met, not just declared" comparing xcodebuild -version against that floor, COVERAGE LOST when xcodebuild is absent; and assert-channel-register.mjs prints no Xcode gap at all. The floor is PINNED AND CHECKED — what stays owner-deferred is the Apple ACCOUNT, not the toolchain. 🔴 THIS TEXT IS READ ALOUD BY CI: assert-legal-tripwires.mjs prints this trigger verbatim on every run, so a stale sentence here is the build asserting an untrue fact about its own state. build-platforms.yml:932 records the SAME sentence being corrected there on 2026-08-20 — one fact in three places, corrected in one. The third copy is Private/requirements/gates.json G9-07.heldReason, which its own evidence field contradicts two lines later.

source.quote: apps uploaded to App Store Connect must be built with Xcode 26 or later — effective 28 April 2026.
